speaker: Narendra Modi
venue: Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, New Delhi
quote_english: Aadhaar has weeded out crores of fake beneficiaries from government schemes (paraphrase from FactChecker's list).
summary: FactChecker rated the claim false: a CAG audit and an RTI reply did not support crores of fake beneficiaries being removed, e.g. only 4% of 9.4 million deleted MGNREGA job cards were fake.

evidence.title: 9 of Prime Minister Modi's 16 claims on schemes true, 3 false
evidence.key_figure: Rated 9 true, 3 false, 2 partly true, 2 unclear across the 30 Nov 2017 HT Leadership Summit speech

evidence.title: Auditor rejects government claims on LPG savings
evidence.key_figure: 74,000 consumer IDs linked to 37,000 Aadhaar numbers; 9.6 lakh ineligible consumers received Rs 49.21 crore

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Rural Development RTI reply (as reported by Hindustan Times)
evidence.title: Nearly a crore fake job cards struck off from MGNREGA
evidence.key_figure: Only 4% of 9.4 million deleted job cards were fake

analysis:
FactChecker examined Modi's statement that Aadhaar weeded out crores of fake beneficiaries and rated it false.

It cited a CAG audit of the LPG subsidy, which found duplicate and ineligible consumer records but not crores of fakes, and an RTI reply showing only about 4% of 9.4 million deleted MGNREGA job cards were fake. The Prime Minister did not say which schemes he meant.

Later versions of the claim (8 crore in 2019, 10 crore in 2023-24) are separate statements and are not assessed here.
notes: The exact wording of the claim is unclear and the verdict rests on the fact-checker's reading. Quote is a paraphrase. The CAG report itself was not opened, only the FactChecker summary.
